==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
{{dercat|en|itc-pro|ine-pro}}
From {{inh|en|enm|chalenge}}, variant with {{l|en|palatalization}} of {{inh|en|enm|kalange||an accusation, claim}}, from {{der|en|fro|chalenge}}, {{m|fro|chalonge}}, palatalized Central French variants of {{der|en|fro-nor|calenge}}, {{m|fro|calonge}} (see Continental Norman [[calengier]]), from {{der|en|la|calumnia||a false accusation, calumny}}. 

Cognate with {{cog|ang|hol#Etymology_2_6|hōl|calumny}}. {{doublet|en|calumny}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈt͡ʃæl.ɪnd͡ʒ/|/ˈt͡ʃæl.ənd͡ʒ/}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-challenge.ogg|a=US}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A [[confrontation]]; a [[dare]].
## An [[antagonization]] or [[instigation]] intended to convince a [[person]] to perform an [[action]] they otherwise would not.
##* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-11-30|volume=409|issue=8864|author=Paul Davis
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/letters/21590879-britain-jfk-assassination-colombia-life-logging-fancy-words Letters: Say it as simply as possible]
|passage=Congratulations on managing to use the phrase “preponderant criterion” in a chart (“[http://www.economist.com/news/united-states/21589427-states-are-starting-test-teachers-your-marks On your marks]”, November 9th). Was this the work of a kakorrhaphiophobic journalist set a '''challenge''' by his colleagues, or simply an example of glossolalia?}}
## A [[bid]] to [[overcome]] something.
##: {{ux|en|a '''challenge''' to the king's authority}}
##* {{quote-web|en|date=May 5, 2012|author=Phil McNulty|work=BBC Sport
|title=[http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/17878435 Chelsea 2-1 Liverpool]
|passage=For Liverpool, their season will now be regarded as a relative disappointment after failure to add the FA Cup to the Carling Cup and not mounting a '''challenge''' to reach the Champions League places.}}
## {{lb|en|sports}} An [[attempt]] to take [[possession]]; a [[tackle]].
##* {{quote-journal|en|date=October 1, 2011|author=Saj Chowdhury|work=BBC Sport
|title=[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/15045306.stm Wolverhampton 1-2 Newcastle]
|passage=Argentine midfielder Jonas Gutierrez added a superb second when he surged past four '''challenges''' to fire in low.}}
## A [[summons]] to fight a [[duel]]; also, the [[letter]] or [[message]] [[convey]]ing the summons.
## The act of a [[sentry]] in [[halt]]ing a person and [[demand]]ing the [[countersign]], or (by extension) the action of a [[computer]] [[system]] demanding a [[password]], etc.
## An attempt to have a [[work]] of [[literature]] [[restrict]]ed or [[remove]]d from a [[public]] [[library]] or [[school]] [[curriculum]].
# A [[difficult]] [[task]], especially one that the person making the attempt finds more [[enjoyable]] because of that difficulty.
# {{lb|en|legal}} A [[procedure]] or [[action]].
## The act of [[appeal]]ing a [[ruling]] or [[decision]] of a [[court]] of [[administrative]] [[agency]].
## {{lb|en|legal|rare}} A [[judge]]'s [[interest]] in the [[result]] of a [[case]], [[constitute|constituting]] grounds for them to not be allowed to [[sit]] the case (e.g., a [[conflict of interest]]).
##: {{ux|en|Consanguinity in direct line is a '''challenge''' for a judge when he or she is sitting cases.}}
## The act of [[seek]]ing to [[remove]] a [[judge]], [[arbitrator]]{{,}} or other [[judicial]] or [[semi-]][[judicial]] figure for reasons of [[alleged]] [[bias]] or [[incapacity]].
##: {{ux|en|We're still waiting to hear how the court rules on our '''challenge''' of the arbitrator based on conflict of interest.}}
## {{lb|en|US}} An act of [[seek]]ing to have a certain person be [[declare]]d not [[legally]] [[qualified]] to [[vote]], made when the person [[offer]]s their [[ballot]].
# {{lb|en|hunting}} The [[open]]ing and [[cry]]ing of [[hound]]s upon first finding the [[scent]] of their [[game]].

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[invite#Verb|invite]] (someone) to take part in a [[competition]].
#: {{ux|en|We '''challenged''' the boys next door to a game of football.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-3|act=IV|scene=iv|passage=By this I '''challenge''' him to single fight.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[dare#Verb|dare]] (someone).
#* {{RQ:Locke Government|chapter=Who Heir?|paragraph=149|page=194|passage=[...] For I '''challenge''' any Man to make any pretence to Power by Right of ''Fatherhood'', either intelligible or poſſible in any one, otherwiſe, then either as ''[[w:Adam|Adams]]'' heir, or as Progenitor over his own deſcendants, naturally ſprung from him.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[dispute#Verb|dispute]] (something); to contest.
#: {{syn|en|call}}
#: {{ux|en|to '''challenge''' the accuracy of a statement or of a quotation}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2022 August 10|author=Dr Mike Esbester|title=New understandings from old incidents|journal=RAIL|issue=963|page=58|text=In the April 2020 Roade fatality, the worker who died "was reputedly in the habit of walking on the line when he didn't need to". Tragically, no one '''challenged''' him about it.}}
# To [[call#Verb|call]] something into [[question]] or [[dispute]].
#: {{ux|en|New information '''challenged''' old hypotheses.}}
# {{lb|en|legal|transitive}} To make a [[formal]] [[objection]] to a [[juror]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To be [[difficult]] or [[challenging]] for.
# {{lb|en|obsolete|transitive}} To [[claim#Verb|claim]] as due; to [[demand#Verb|demand]] as a right.
#* {{RQ:Addison Cato|7|passage='''Challenge''' better terms.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete|transitive}} To [[censure]]; to [[blame#Verb|blame]].
#* {{RQ:Pliny Holland Historie of the World
|passage=I may be more '''challenged''' for my inconsiderate Boldness}}
# {{lb|en|military|transitive}} To [[question#Verb|question]] or demand the [[countersign]] from (one who attempts to pass the lines).
#: {{ux|en|The sentinel '''challenged''' us with "Who goes there?"}}
# {{lb|en|US|transitive}} To [[object#Verb|object]] to the reception of the [[vote]] of, e.g. on the ground that the person is not qualified as a voter.
# {{lb|en|Canada|US|transitive}} To take (a final exam) in order to get credit for a course without taking it.
